title: HB884 (2020 Regular): RELATING TO FIREARMS.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Hawaii) (gun-policy Stage 5, Hawaii); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Hawaii text (Introduced, official copy, https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/session2020/bills/HB884_.HTM; sha256 b0bb29ea0941ced2bc5d493edf379013bc2ee9f8980fc40380d674db3d507e6a)
provenance.note: As-filed text; no passage vote on file. The bill strikes the limit of a license to the county where it is granted (concealed and unconcealed carry) and the one-year expiry. Quotes leave out the struck words.

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (HRS 134-9): In an exceptional case, when an applicant shows reason to fear injury to the applicant's person or property, the chief of police of the appropriate county may grant a license to an applicant who is a citizen of the United States of the age of twenty-one years or more or to a duly accredited official representative of a foreign nation of the age of twenty-one years or more to carry a pistol or revolver and ammunition therefor concealed on the person within the State.
SECTION 1 (HRS 134-9): Unless renewed, the license shall expire five years from the date of issue.
